checks.explanation: US CPI inflation did not sustainably return to 2% for an extended period; it hovered in the roughly 2.5-3.5% range through much of 2024-2026, broadly matching the prediction of persistent ~3% inflation.

Some sectors began showing measurable AI ROI (coding productivity, customer service automation) by 2025-2026, though broad, unambiguous proof that AI infrastructure investment overall was 'economically justified' remained a debated, unresolved question.

The AI and startup funding markets did go through a notable shakeout period in the following year, with weaker AI startups struggling to raise follow-on funding while capital concentrated in a smaller set of well-funded frontier labs.

Apple Intelligence's rollout with the iPhone 16 was delayed and phased, and while iPhone 16 sales were solid, it did not trigger the outsized 'everyone upgrades' supercycle originally predicted; Apple's AI features received mixed early reviews.

Next-generation LLMs released roughly a year later (GPT-4o, Claude 3.5, and subsequent models) showed substantial quality improvements over mid-2024 models, broadly consistent with reaching a much higher output quality tier.
AI-driven labor arbitrage and productivity tools saw substantial adoption growth through 2025, with many organizations reporting meaningful efficiency gains from AI tooling.

Tesla's Optimus and comparable humanoid robots remained far more expensive than $20,000 per unit as of 2025-2026, with actual commercial pricing (where announced) running into the tens of thousands of dollars or higher and mass consumer availability not yet achieved.

France's fragmented 2024 National Assembly did produce significant political gridlock, including government collapses and an inability to pass major reform agendas, consistent with the predicted logjam.

No definitive whistleblower emerged within ten days of this episode alleging a cover-up of Biden's cognitive decline; Biden's withdrawal in July 2024 was driven primarily by the fallout from his poor June 27 debate performance and mounting party pressure, not a specific whistleblower revelation.

No major Watergate-style investigative leak exposing a organized cover-up of Biden's condition emerged before the election in the dramatic form predicted; while media scrutiny of Biden's fitness increased after the debate, it was not framed as a clandestine insider leak of that magnitude.
Biden ultimately withdrew from the race in July 2024 rather than facing Trump directly, and Democrats effectively did organize a compressed process to elevate Kamala Harris as the new nominee.

Biden did not withdraw by August 19 (he withdrew July 21, 2024, earlier than predicted), and no specific whistleblower emerged in July 2024 as predicted, though the broader 'speedrun' replacement dynamic did occur.
When Biden withdrew in July 2024, Democrats did not hold an open primary; the party quickly consolidated behind Kamala Harris as the nominee, exactly as predicted.
